To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the promoter regions for cell-cycle regulated genes contain a number of conserved motifs, and these motifs are enriched in a subset of the genes with the same expression profile.

(1) the promoter regions of co-expressed genes contain more similar sequence elements than expected by chance, (2) the sequence elements are not random but tend to be clustered in certain regions of the promoter regions, and (3) these sequence elements are not randomly distributed among the co-expressed genes but tend to be concentrated in certain groups of co-expressed gene clusters.

the cell-cycle regulated genes in S. cerevisiae are organized into a number of distinct clusters of functionally related genes, that the promoters of these clusters contain a number of common regulatory DNA sequence motifs, and that these motifs may be used to predict new members of the cell-cycle regulated gene clusters.
